svg.text: OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code + PKCE, with an email one-time code as a second factor. Every arrow is a real request; the panel at the foot lists what makes each step fail.
code_challenge = S256(code_verifier); both kept in sessionStorage
filtered: only GET navigations; /oauth2/authorize always kept
CRITICAL tier: 5/min per IP, submissions only
single use, TTL 5 min, bounded attempts
park Authentication + email in session; clear SecurityContext
user is deliberately anonymous again until the code is verified
restore parked Authentication; saveContext; consume saved request
restored, not rebuilt: a fresh token loses authenticationTime
replay saved request; validate client, redirect_uri, PKCE
5 - CODE EXCHANGE AND FIRST API CALL
mismatch -> aborts before any network call
needs auth_time from the restored Authentication
Where it breaks — and what it looks like
CRITICAL tier exhausted, or an escalating block still counting down
LoginAttemptService records it; progressive lock after N failures
challenge survives; burned once the attempt bound is passed
the code was already consumed, so no pending challenge remains
the SPA origin must be listed, or the browser drops the redirect silently
an older authorize request resumed, carrying a state the SPA no longer holds
Security 7 protects API endpoints by default; the client cannot send a token
a hand-made token has no authentication time for the auth_time claim
